items.question: Do I need travel insurance and permits?
answer: Yes. Both are required, and neither is optional.
Travel insurance is mandatory and must cover:
list: High-altitude travel above 5,000 metres
Motorcycle riding, which many standard policies exclude
Emergency evacuation, including by helicopter
after: The Himalayas are remote. Proper cover is what stands between an incident and a very expensive problem.
Permits are required for several regions, including Ladakh. We arrange all of them, but we need your passport and visa details well in advance to do it.

items.question: When is the riding season in the Indian Himalayas?
answer: Broadly June to September, and the edges of that window move every year with the snow.
list: June: passes open, rivers running high from the melt
July and August: the most reliable riding, though the monsoon affects the approach through Himachal
September: clear skies and the best light, with cold nights
after: Outside that window most high passes are closed. We will tell you if your dates do not work rather than sell you a trip that will not run.

items.question: What licence do I need to ride in India?
answer: You need a valid motorcycle licence from your home country plus an International Driving Permit, obtained before you travel. An IDP is not issued in India.
Bring the physical documents. A photograph on your phone will not satisfy a checkpoint.

items.question: What are the Himalayas?
answer: The Himalayas are the highest mountain range on earth, running across India, Nepal, Bhutan, China and Pakistan, and forming the barrier between the Indian subcontinent and the Tibetan Plateau.
The range holds Mount Everest and more than a hundred peaks above 7,000 metres. The Indus, Ganges and Brahmaputra all rise here and support hundreds of millions of people downstream.
For anyone travelling by motorcycle or 4x4, the appeal is the combination of:
list: High mountain passes, several of them among the highest roads in the world
Remote off-road trails with days between settlements
Landscapes that shift from glacier to cold desert within a single day
Living Hindu and Buddhist cultures, not preserved ones
after: We run expeditions in the Indian, Nepalese and Bhutanese Himalayas.

items.question: Why are the Himalayas the best place for a motorcycle expedition?
answer: Because few places combine this much altitude, this much remoteness and this much variety in a single trip.
Riders get a mix of tarmac, gravel and genuine off-road, on roads that climb past 5,000 metres and through country that sees very few vehicles. Each region reads differently:
list: Ladakh: high passes and extreme, arid landscapes
Spiti Valley: remote, raw and technically harder than it looks
Upper Mustang in Nepal: trans-Himalayan desert and Tibetan culture
Bhutan: quieter roads, dense forest and a slower pace
after: The riding alone would justify the trip. The monasteries, villages and the sheer scale of the place are what people talk about afterwards.

items.question: Is it safe to ride in the Himalayas?
answer: Yes, when the expedition is planned and staffed properly. The risk here is not the road, it is being unprepared for altitude and distance.
Every expedition travels with an expedition leader, riding guides, a mechanic and a backup vehicle. We also run:
list: Acclimatisation days before anyone rides high
Daily checks on how each rider is coping with altitude
Oxygen and first aid carried at all times
Routes built from experience rather than from a map
after: The single most effective safety measure is a schedule with enough slack that nobody feels pressure to ride while unwell.

items.question: How difficult are Himalayan expeditions?
answer: Moderate to challenging, depending on the route.
Expect:
list: Long riding days between 3,000 and 5,800 metres
A mix of smooth tarmac and genuine off-road
Weather that can change within an hour
Remote sections with no fuel, food or signal
after: They suit riders with basic to intermediate experience and reasonable fitness. With a structured itinerary and a support team, most riders complete the route comfortably.

items.question: Do I need travel insurance and permits?
answer: Yes. Both are required for every Himalayan expedition.
Travel insurance is mandatory and must cover:
list: High-altitude travel above 5,000 metres
Motorcycle riding, which many standard policies exclude
Emergency evacuation, including by helicopter
after: These are remote regions and evacuation is expensive. Check the exclusions on your policy rather than assuming.
Permits are required for several regions including Ladakh. We arrange all of them, but we need your passport and visa details in advance.

intro.focus: Our expeditions run through the Nepalese Himalayas, from Kathmandu up the Kali Gandaki into Mustang. It is the same range we have worked since 2014, read from the other side of the border.

items.question: Do I need permits to ride in Nepal?
answer: Yes, and Upper Mustang needs more than the usual ones.
Depending on the route, expect to need:
list: A restricted area permit for Upper Mustang, which can only be issued through a registered agency
An Annapurna Conservation Area permit
A tourist visa, available on arrival for most nationalities
after: We arrange the permits, but the restricted area one takes time and needs your passport and visa details well before departure. Leave it late and the route has to change.

items.question: When is the riding season in Nepal?
answer: Spring and autumn are the main windows, and Mustang stretches them.
list: March to May: warm, clear, rhododendron in flower at altitude
June to August: monsoon in most of the country, but Mustang sits in the rain shadow and stays comparatively dry
September to November: the most settled weather and the sharpest mountain views
after: December to February is cold and several passes get snow. Tell us your dates and we will say honestly whether they work.

items.question: What licence do I need to ride in Nepal?
answer: A valid motorcycle licence from your home country plus an International Driving Permit, obtained before you travel.
Bring the physical documents. Checkpoints on the Mustang road do ask.

items.question: What is Upper Mustang?
answer: Upper Mustang is the northern half of Nepal's Mustang district, a high desert valley that sits behind the main Himalayan range and opens onto the Tibetan Plateau.
It was a separate kingdom, Lo, until 2008, and closed to outsiders until 1992. The culture, the architecture and the language are Tibetan rather than Nepali, and Lo Manthang is still a walled city.
For a rider, it means:
list: Ochre canyon country with almost no vegetation
Roads cut into cliffs above the Kali Gandaki
Villages and monasteries that have changed very little
Dry air, hard light and a wind that gets up every afternoon
after: It is the closest thing to riding in Tibet without crossing the border.

items.question: What is the Kali Gandaki gorge?
answer: The Kali Gandaki river cuts between Annapurna and Dhaulagiri, both over 8,000 metres, and the gap between the peaks and the riverbed makes it the deepest gorge on earth by most measures.
The road follows the riverbed for much of the way. You ride out of forest into desert in a single day, with the two massifs directly overhead.

items.question: How difficult is the riding?
answer: Moderate. Less technical than Ladakh, but longer on unsealed surfaces.
list: Sealed road from Kathmandu to Pokhara and beyond
Gravel, riverbed and loose surfaces north of Jomsom
A strong headwind up the valley most afternoons
Altitude around 3,000 to 4,000 metres in Mustang, higher on side trips
after: It suits riders with basic to intermediate off-road experience. The wind is what tires people, not the terrain, which is why the riding day ends early.

items.question: Is it safe to ride in Nepal?
answer: Yes, with a properly staffed expedition. The risks are altitude, weather and the state of the road after monsoon, and all three are managed by planning rather than by riding skill.
Every expedition travels with an expedition leader, riding guides, a mechanic and a backup vehicle. We also run:
list: Acclimatisation days before anyone rides high
Daily checks on how each rider is coping with altitude
Oxygen and first aid carried at all times
Routes built from experience rather than from a map
after: Mustang is remote. Evacuation from there is by helicopter, which is one reason insurance is not optional.

items.question: Do I need travel insurance?
answer: Yes. It is mandatory, and it must cover:
list: High-altitude travel above 4,000 metres
Motorcycle riding, which many standard policies exclude
Emergency evacuation, including by helicopter
after: Check the exclusions on your policy rather than assuming. Helicopter evacuation from Mustang is expensive and uninsured riders have found that out the hard way.

bhutan.title: Motorcycle expeditions across Bhutan
bhutan.lead: Paro to Punakha over the Dochula pass, then east into valleys most visitors never reach. Bhutan is small, green and steep, and the roads were built to follow the rivers rather than to save time.

intro.title: The eastern Himalaya, at a slower pace.
intro.body: Bhutan sits at the wet end of the range. Instead of the bare high desert of Ladakh you get pine and rhododendron forest, cloud sitting in the valleys until mid morning, and passes strung with prayer flags at 3,000 metres. The riding is not extreme, but it is nearly all corners.
intro.focus: Our route runs the western and central valleys, from Paro and Thimphu over Dochula into Punakha and on towards Phobjikha and Bumthang. Every visitor here travels with a licensed operator, so the paperwork is part of the trip rather than an afterthought.

items.question: Can I ride my own motorcycle in Bhutan?
answer: Foreign visitors ride with a licensed operator, and most of our riders take one of our bikes.
If you want to bring your own, expect to arrange:
list: A temporary import permit for the motorcycle, applied for in advance
A route permit covering every district you pass through
Third party insurance valid inside Bhutan
after: Tell us early if this is what you want. It is possible, but it changes the timeline and the paperwork.

items.question: When is the riding season in Bhutan?
answer: Spring and autumn, either side of the monsoon.
list: March to May: rhododendron in flower, warm days, some haze
June to August: heavy monsoon rain and landslides on the east west highway
September to November: the clearest skies of the year and the main festival season
after: Winter riding is possible in the lower valleys but the high passes get snow. Send us your dates and we will say honestly whether they work.

easternHimalayas.card: Paro, Thimphu, the Dochula pass and the Punakha valley. Forested passes, dzongs and quiet roads, ridden in spring and autumn.

meta.title: Motorcycle Tours Across Sri Lanka | Offhorizon
meta.description: Guided motorcycle tours in Sri Lanka. The hill country, Sigiriya, Ella and the south coast, with guides, mechanic and a backup vehicle on every departure.

sriLanka.title: Motorcycle tours across Sri Lanka
sriLanka.lead: Tea estates above 1,800 metres, ancient rock forts, and a coast road you can ride with the sea on one side the whole way. Sri Lanka is the warm counterweight to a Himalayan season.

intro.title: A small island with three climates on it.
intro.body: You can leave the coast in the morning at thirty degrees and be pulling on a jacket in the tea country by lunch. The hill roads between Kandy, Nuwara Eliya and Ella are tight, cool and green, and the coastal stretches in the south are as easy as riding gets.
intro.focus: Our route links the cultural triangle around Sigiriya, the central hill country, and the southern coast. It is a good first expedition, and a good one to bring a pillion on.

regions.title: Where we ride in Sri Lanka

why.title: Why ride Sri Lanka with Offhorizon

reasons.title: Routes we have ridden
reasons.body: No line drawn on a map in an office. Every day of this one has been ridden before you get it.

reasons.title: Roads, not highways
reasons.body: The island is easy to cross quickly and much better slowly. We take the hill roads.

reasons.title: Local guides
reasons.body: Sri Lankan guides who know which estate road is open and where lunch is actually worth stopping for.

reasons.title: Full support
reasons.body: Expedition leader, mechanic travelling with the group and a backup vehicle carrying spares and luggage.

why.closing: Small groups. We would rather run one good departure than three crowded ones.

cta.title: Start your Sri Lanka tour
cta.body: Pick a departure from the calendar, or tell us the dates you have and we will build the route around them.
cta.imageAlt: Tea plantation on the slopes above Nuwara Eliya in the Sri Lankan hill country

items.question: What licence do I need to ride in Sri Lanka?
answer: A motorcycle licence from home, an International Driving Permit, and a local recognition permit.
The local permit is issued in Colombo by the Automobile Association of Ceylon against your IDP. We handle it on arrival, but bring the physical documents with you.

items.question: When is the riding season in Sri Lanka?
answer: Two monsoons hit opposite sides of the island, so something is usually dry.
list: December to March: best for the south and west coasts and the hill country
May to September: wet in the southwest, dry in the north and east
April and October: the changeover months, mixed weather anywhere
after: Our departures sit in the December to March window. Send us other dates and we will tell you what the weather is likely to do.

hillCountry.card: Kandy, Nuwara Eliya and Ella, with Sigiriya and the south coast either side. Tea estates, tight mountain roads and warm winter riding.

meta.title: Motorcycle and 4x4 Expeditions Across Mongolia | Offhorizon
meta.description: Guided motorcycle and 4x4 expeditions in Mongolia. The steppe, the Gobi and the Altai, with guides, mechanic, support vehicle and camp equipment carried.

mongolia.title: Motorcycle and 4x4 expeditions across Mongolia
mongolia.lead: Grassland to the horizon, sand and rock in the Gobi, and glaciers in the Altai. Mongolia has almost no tarmac outside the capital, which is the entire point of going.

intro.title: The country with the fewest roads and the most riding.
intro.body: Once you leave Ulaanbaatar the road becomes a set of tracks going roughly the same way, and choosing between them is the day's work. Distances are long, fuel stops are far apart, and you camp where the light runs out.
intro.focus: We run both a motorcycle expedition and a 4x4 expedition here, through the central steppe and south into the Gobi, with the Altai as the longer option. This is the most remote thing on our calendar and it is planned that way.

why.title: Why ride Mongolia with Offhorizon

reasons.title: Remote by design
reasons.body: Fuel, water, spares and food planned around days where there is nothing to buy.

reasons.title: Navigation that works
reasons.body: Tracked routes, satellite communication and a leader who knows which braid of the track goes through.

reasons.title: Local guides
reasons.body: Mongolian guides and drivers who grew up on this ground and know where the river is fordable.

reasons.title: Full support
reasons.body: Expedition leader, mechanic, support vehicle carrying camp equipment, spares and luggage.

why.closing: Small groups. We would rather run one good departure than three crowded ones.

cta.title: Start your Mongolia expedition
cta.body: Pick a departure from the calendar, or tell us the dates you have and we will build the route around them.
cta.imageAlt: Gers and open grassland on the Mongolian steppe

items.question: How hard is the riding in Mongolia?
answer: Not technical, but long, loose and tiring. Expect gravel, sand, corrugations and river crossings.
You should be comfortable riding off tarmac all day and picking a bike up. It is not the place to learn, and we will say so if the expedition is not right for you.

items.question: Where do we sleep?
answer: A mix, and the balance shifts with the route.
list: Ger camps where there are any, which is most nights on the central steppe
Tents carried in the support vehicle on the remote sections
Hotels at either end of the trip in Ulaanbaatar
after: Sleeping bags rated for cold nights are worth bringing. The steppe drops close to freezing even in summer.

items.question: When is the riding season in Mongolia?
answer: June to September, and that window is firm.
July and August are the warmest and the greenest. June and September are colder and quieter. Outside those months the ground freezes and the tracks are not passable.

steppeGobi.card: Central steppe, the Gobi and the Altai. Almost no tarmac, long days on tracks, and camping where the light runs out.

tibetPlateau.card: Kathmandu to the base camps below Everest and Cho Oyu, across a plateau that runs high, wide and empty. October and November only.

meta.title: Motorcycle Expeditions Across Tibet | Offhorizon
meta.description: Ride from Kathmandu across the Tibetan plateau to the base camps below Everest and Cho Oyu. Permits, a border crossing and an acclimatisation plan, all handled.

tibet.title: Motorcycle expeditions across Tibet
tibet.lead: Most people see Everest from a trekking trail. On this side of the border you ride to it, across a plateau that runs wide, high and almost empty for three hundred kilometres at a stretch.

intro.title: The highest road riding on earth.
intro.body: Tibet is not a harder ride than Ladakh, it is a bigger one. The tarmac out of Kyirong is good and the passes are graded, but you spend days above 14,000 feet with the wind coming across open ground and nothing between one town and the next. What makes it serious is the altitude, the distance and the weather, in that order.
intro.focus: Our route crosses at Rasuwagadhi and runs the Friendship Highway past Peiku Tso, under Shishapangma and Cho Oyu, to the base camps and back. Every rider needs a Tibet travel permit and a group visa, both arranged through our Lhasa-registered partner, and Chinese law requires a registered guide and vehicle with the group the whole way.

why.title: Why ride Tibet with Offhorizon

reasons.title: Both sides of the border
reasons.body: A Kathmandu team and a Lhasa-registered partner, so the crossing at Rasuwagadhi is a morning rather than an ordeal.

reasons.title: Permits, not promises
reasons.body: The Tibet travel permit and the group visa take a working day in Kathmandu and cannot be rushed. It is built into the itinerary.

reasons.title: Altitude taken slowly
reasons.body: Kyirong, then Tingri, then the base camps. Oxygen, a first aid kit and an altitude protocol travel with the group.

reasons.title: Full support
reasons.body: Expedition leader, road captain, sweep rider, mechanic and a backup vehicle carrying the luggage.

why.closing: Ten riders at most. On ground this remote, a bigger group is a slower group.

cta.title: Start your Tibet expedition
cta.body: October and November are the settled months. Tell us which one and we will start the paperwork.
cta.imageAlt: The Friendship Highway climbing across the Tibetan plateau

items.question: What permits do I need for Tibet?
answer: More than anywhere else we ride, and none of them can be bought at the border.
For this expedition you need:
list: A Tibet travel permit, issued only through a registered agency in Lhasa
A Chinese group visa, applied for in Kathmandu rather than at home
An alien travel permit for the sections beyond Tingri
A registered Chinese guide and vehicle with the group, which the law requires
after: We arrange all of it, and the itinerary gives it a full working day in Kathmandu. Your passport has to be with us for that day, so do not plan anything that needs it.

items.question: How high does this expedition go?
answer: The base camp day tops out around 16,000 feet, and you sleep at 14,268 feet at Tingri for two nights.

That is high enough that acclimatisation is not optional. We climb in stages, ride the plateau days slowly, and carry oxygen. If someone is not adjusting, the answer is to lose altitude, and the backup vehicle is there for exactly that.

items.question: When can this expedition run?
answer: October and November, and there is little flexibility in that.
list: October: the clearest skies of the year and the sharpest views of the north faces
November: colder, quieter, still clear, and the last of the season
December to April: the plateau is bitter and the border regularly closes
May to September: the monsoon on the Nepal side and cloud over the mountains
after: The border itself can also close at short notice for reasons that have nothing to do with weather. It is the one risk on this route we cannot plan away.

terms.title: Terms of service
terms.lead: The agreement between you and Offhorizon Adventures when you book an expedition with us. Plain English, and short enough to read.

meta.title: Terms of Service | Offhorizon Adventures
meta.description: Booking terms for Offhorizon Adventures expeditions: payment, cancellation, what we provide, what you bring, and where you stand if a route has to change.

sections.title: Who you are booking with
body: Offhorizon Adventures runs guided motorcycle and 4x4 expeditions from Log Huts Rd, Siyal, Manali, Himachal Pradesh 175131, India. In these terms, we and us mean Offhorizon Adventures, and you means the person making the booking and everyone named on it.
Booking an expedition means you have read these terms and accepted them on behalf of everyone in your party.

sections.title: Booking and payment
body: A booking is confirmed when we have written to you to confirm it and the first payment has reached us. Until both have happened, the place is not held.
You choose how to pay. Either settle the whole expedition at once, or pay 20 percent to hold your place and clear the rest before you travel.
Places come off sale 30 days before departure. After that the group is closed, the permits are filed and we cannot add anyone.
list: The 20 percent is due at the time of booking and is what confirms the place
The balance can be paid in as many instalments as you like, of any amount, whenever suits you
Everything must be paid no later than 14 days before the departure date
Prices are set in Indian rupees and charged in your own currency at the rate on the day you book, which is then fixed for the rest of the booking
after: Flights are never included. Nothing you pay is refundable, so please read what the expedition involves before you book.

sections.title: Changing your booking
body: Tell us as early as you can and we will do what we can. Moving to another departure of the same expedition is usually possible more than 45 days out, subject to space and to any cost we have already committed on your behalf.
A name change is normally straightforward, but permits for restricted areas are issued against a passport and cannot always be reissued in time.

sections.title: If you cancel
body: Cancellations must reach us in writing. The date we receive your written notice is the date we use.

Money paid towards an expedition is not refundable, at any point. It pays for permits, rooms, vehicles and bookings we commit to as soon as you book, and we cannot get those back. Insurance that covers cancellation is worth having, and we say so on every booking.
after: If you cannot travel, ask us about moving to another departure before you cancel. More than 45 days out and with space on the other date, that is usually possible.

sections.title: If the balance is not paid in time
body: Fourteen days before departure is a hard line, not a reminder. Permits are filed, rooms are paid for and vehicles are committed against that date.

If anything is still outstanding when it passes, the booking is cancelled, the documents form is withdrawn, the place goes back on sale and no money is returned. We would much rather this never happened, so we write to you as the date approaches, and if you are in difficulty, tell us early and we will do what we can.

sections.title: If we change or cancel
body: Mountain routes change. Landslides, snow, closed passes, weather and permit decisions are outside our control, and your expedition leader may alter the route, the order of days or the accommodation to keep the group moving and safe. We will always aim to give you an expedition of the same standard.

If we cancel an expedition outright for a reason within our control, you may take a full refund or transfer to another departure. Every expedition needs a minimum number of riders, and if that number is not reached we will tell you at least 30 days before departure and offer the same choice.

sections.title: What you need to bring
body: Some things only you can arrange, and without them you cannot ride. Please check them early rather than the week before.
list: A valid motorcycle licence from your home country and an International Driving Permit, both as physical documents
A passport valid for at least six months after your return date, and the correct visa
Travel insurance covering motorcycling, off road driving and evacuation at the altitudes on your route
Your own riding gear, unless we have agreed otherwise in writing

sections.title: Riding, risk and the group
body: Riding at altitude on unsealed mountain roads carries risk that no amount of planning removes. You take part knowing that, and you are responsible for riding within your ability and for the condition you turn up in.

The expedition leader's decision is final on safety, on route changes and on whether a rider continues. We may remove someone from an expedition, without refund, for riding dangerously, for riding under the influence of alcohol or drugs, or for behaviour that puts the group at risk.

sections.title: Our liability
body: We are responsible for running the expedition described in your confirmation with reasonable care and skill. We are not responsible for loss or injury caused by your own actions, by a third party unconnected with the expedition, or by events we could not have foreseen or avoided, including weather, landslide, road closure, strike, civil unrest and government decisions.
Nothing in these terms limits liability for death or personal injury caused by our negligence, or for anything else that cannot be limited by law.

sections.title: Complaints, law and jurisdiction
body: If something is wrong, tell your expedition leader while you are still on the road, when it can usually be fixed. If it cannot be settled there, write to us within 28 days of getting home and we will answer within 28 days.
These terms are governed by the law of India, and the courts of Himachal Pradesh have jurisdiction.

privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.lead: What we collect when you enquire, book or make an account, why we hold it, and how to get it back or have it deleted.

meta.title: Privacy Policy | Offhorizon Adventures
meta.description: How Offhorizon Adventures collects, uses and protects your personal data, who we share it with, how long we keep it, and how to exercise your rights.

sections.title: What we collect
body: Only what we need to answer you and to run your expedition. We do not buy lists and we do not sell anything about you.
list: Contact details you give us: name, email address, phone number and country
Enquiry content: the dates, routes and questions you send us
Booking details: the travellers on the booking, dates, room and vehicle choices, licence and passport details where a permit needs them
Account details if you make one, including how you signed in with Google or Facebook
Technical data your browser sends: IP address, device and pages visited

sections.title: Why we use it
body: To reply to enquiries, to quote and confirm bookings, to apply for the permits your route needs, to take payment, and to tell you about changes to a departure you are on.
We use Google Tag Manager and Google Analytics to count visits and see which pages are read. Nothing analytical is loaded until you agree to it, and we do not use any of it to build a profile of you.

sections.title: The basis we rely on
body: For enquiries and bookings, we process your data because it is necessary to take steps at your request and to perform our contract with you.

For permits and for records we are required to keep, we rely on our legal obligations. For anything else, such as marketing email, we rely on your consent, and you can withdraw it at any time without giving a reason.

sections.title: Who else sees it
body: Only the people needed to deliver the expedition, and only what they need.
list: Hotels, guesthouses and camps on your route, for the rooms in your name
Government departments that issue restricted area and route permits
Razorpay, our payment provider, which handles card details directly so we never hold them
ipapi.co, which turns your address into a country once so prices can be shown in your currency
Google, through Tag Manager and Analytics, which receives the pages you visited once you have agreed to it
Supabase, which hosts our database and sign in, and our email provider
Professional advisers or authorities where the law requires it
Other riders on your booking, who see the names of the group they were invited to join

sections.title: Where it is held, and for how long
body: Data is held on servers operated by our hosting providers, which may be inside or outside your country. Where data leaves the European Economic Area we rely on the standard contractual clauses.

Enquiries are kept for two years. Booking records, invoices and payment records are kept for eight years, which is the period Indian tax law requires. Account data is kept until you delete the account.

sections.title: Your rights
body: You can ask for a copy of what we hold, ask us to correct it, ask us to delete it, object to how we use it, or ask us to send it to someone else. We answer within 30 days and there is no charge.
You can delete your account yourself at any time from inside the account. If you are in the European Union or the United Kingdom, you may also complain to your national data protection authority.

sections.title: Cookies and what your browser stores
body: We do not use advertising cookies and we do not track you across other sites.

Your browser stores three things: the language you chose, a cookie named oh_country holding the country we looked up once so prices can be shown in your currency, and, if you sign in, a session so you stay signed in. Clearing your browser storage removes all of it.
If you agree to analytics, Google Analytics also sets its own cookies. Until you do, none are written.

sections.title: Changes and how to reach us
body: If this policy changes we will update the date at the top of this page, and we will tell you directly if the change affects how we use data you have already given us.
The person responsible for data at Offhorizon Adventures can be reached at Log Huts Rd, Siyal, Manali, Himachal Pradesh 175131, India, or by email.

bookingGuide.title: How booking works
bookingGuide.lead: Five minutes of reading that saves a difficult conversation later. There is one deadline that matters, and everything else is straightforward.
bookingGuide.stepsTitle: From picking a date to being on the start line

steps.title: Pick the expedition and the date
steps.body: Open the dates on any expedition page and choose a departure. You will see how many places are left on it, and the price for the party you are bringing before you pay anything.

steps.title: Say who is coming
steps.body: Riders, pillions, single rooms, damage protection, and on a 4x4 expedition the car you want or your own. The total changes as you choose, so nothing is a surprise.

steps.title: Pay in full, or pay 20 percent
steps.body: Either settles the place. Paying in full is done with it; paying 20 percent holds the place and leaves the rest to clear before you travel.

steps.title: The place is yours
steps.body: A confirmation email arrives with your booking reference, and the booking appears in your account with everything paid and everything still outstanding.

steps.title: Send your documents
steps.body: Once the expedition is paid for in full, a form appears on your account. Licence, passport, insurance and the details we need for permits. Fill it in, then mark it as sent so we both know where we stand.

steps.title: Ride
steps.body: We are in touch before departure with the meeting point, the weather and anything the route is doing that week.

deadline.title: Everything must be paid 14 days before departure
body: That date is not a reminder. Permits are filed against it, rooms are paid for and vehicles are committed, and none of it can be undone at short notice.
If anything is still outstanding when it passes, the booking is cancelled, the documents form is withdrawn and the place goes back on sale. Money already paid is not returned.

We write to you as the date comes closer, and your account shows what is left at all times. If you are in difficulty, tell us early: there is a great deal we can do two months out and very little we can do two weeks out.

sections.title: Paying the balance in instalments
body: There is no schedule to keep to. Once the 20 percent is paid, you can pay whatever you like, whenever you like, as many times as you like, until the balance is clear.
Open the booking in your account, type an amount and pay it. The balance updates immediately and the receipt is emailed to you.

sections.title: Booking for more than one rider
body: Book and pay for as many riders as you are bringing, and you will get an invite link for each of the others.
Send the link to each rider. They make an account, join the group, and their own documents form appears for them to fill in. They see the expedition and the group, not what anyone paid.
Pillions do not need an invite or an account: name them on the booking and we have what we need.

sections.title: What we charge, and in what currency
body: Prices are set in Indian rupees and shown to you in your own currency. You are charged in your own currency where our payment provider can take it, and in rupees where it cannot.
The rate is fixed the moment you book. A booking paid across four instalments over five months is settled at the rate on the day it was made, not the rate on the day each instalment lands.

sections.title: Custom expeditions
body: A custom expedition is built for you and only appears in your account. Choose your riders and pillions, and pay in full or with 20 percent exactly as above.
Only the person the expedition was built for can pay for it. Everyone else joins through the invite link and fills in their documents.

sections.title: Is any of it refundable?
body: No. Money paid towards an expedition is not refundable at any point, because it goes straight out again on permits, rooms and vehicles that cannot be recovered.

Travel insurance that covers cancellation is worth having, and we recommend it on every booking. If you cannot travel, ask us about moving to another departure before you cancel: more than 45 days out and with space on the other date, that is usually possible.
